title: Fatal cougar attack on mountain bikers near North Bend, Washington
summary: Two mountain bikers encountered a cougar in the foothills near North Bend, about 30 miles east of Seattle. S.J. Brooks, 32, was killed; another rider was seriously injured. Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife officers later tracked and killed the animal.
attribution: Contemporary news reports (AP). Not official agency data.

sources.title: 1 dead, 1 injured in cougar attack in Washington state

title: Fatal cougar attack on Hunchback Mountain Trail, Oregon
summary: Diana Bober, 55, was killed by a cougar on the Hunchback Mountain Trail in Mount Hood National Forest — reported as Oregon’s first recorded fatal cougar attack.
attribution: Public fatal-cougar compilation and contemporary reporting.

sources.title: List of fatal cougar attacks in North America

title: Fatal mountain lion attack on brothers near Georgetown, California
summary: Taylen Robert Claude Brooks, 21, was killed and his 18-year-old brother Wyatt was gravely injured while looking for shed antlers in a remote wooded area near Georgetown. Authorities described it as California’s first fatal mountain-lion attack in about 20 years.
attribution: Reuters / Los Angeles Times / El Dorado County Sheriff’s Office reporting.

sources.title: Mountain lion kills man, injures brother in rare California fatal attack

title: Trail runner fights off mountain lion near Fort Collins, Colorado
summary: Travis Kauffman, 31, was attacked by a juvenile mountain lion while trail running west of Fort Collins. He fought the cat with his hands, feet, and a rock, eventually suffocating it. He was treated for bites and scratches.
attribution: Colorado Parks and Wildlife / contemporary news.

sources.title: Update on Larimer County mountain lion attack

title: Five-year-old injured in mountain lion attack near Lake Forest, California
summary: Mark Reynolds, 35, was killed by a mountain lion while mountain biking at Whiting Ranch. The same animal later attacked a young girl who survived. The lion was tracked and killed.

sources.title: List of fatal cougar attacks in North America

title: Jogger killed by mountain lion on Auburn trail, California
summary: Barbara Schoener, 40, was killed by a mountain lion while jogging on a trail near Auburn in the Sierra Nevada foothills — one of California’s best-known modern fatal cougar cases.

sources.title: List of fatal cougar attacks in North America

title: Child injured in cougar attack near Olympia, Washington
summary: A 5-year-old boy was bitten on the head by a cougar while walking with family in Capitol State Forest. Adults drove the animal off. WDFW later euthanized a cougar in the area.

sources.title: Update on Capitol Forest cougar incident
sources.publisher: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

title: Hiker injured in mountain lion encounter, Boulder, Colorado
summary: A mountain lion injured a hiker on a trail west of Boulder. Colorado Parks and Wildlife investigated and later killed a lion matching the description after public-safety concerns.

title: Cyclist injured in cougar attack near Canmore, Alberta
summary: A cougar injured a person in the Canmore / Bow Valley area of Alberta during winter recreation. Provincial wildlife officers responded; Bow Valley has recurring cougar activity near town.

title: Elk gores visitor in Estes Park, Colorado
summary: During the fall rut, a bull elk gored a visitor in Estes Park after people approached too closely for photographs — a recurring pattern in Rocky Mountain National Park gateway towns.

title: Elk attack on visitor near Mammoth, Yellowstone
summary: A cow or bull elk (rut / calf-defense season) injured a visitor who approached in the Mammoth developed area. NPS repeatedly warns that elk cause more injuries in some years than bears inside Yellowstone.

title: Cow elk charges photographer in Banff townsite
summary: A cow elk with a calf charged a person photographing wildlife too closely in the Banff townsite. Parks Canada regularly closes areas and issues warnings during calving and rut.

title: Bull elk injures tourist in Jasper, Alberta
summary: During the September rut, a bull elk injured a tourist who approached for a photo in Jasper National Park. Parks Canada cites elk as a leading cause of human-wildlife conflict injuries in mountain parks.

title: Elk knocks down visitor on a Rocky Mountain NP roadside
summary: A visitor who left a vehicle to photograph a bull elk during the rut was knocked down. NPS reminds visitors to stay at least 25 yards from elk and 100 yards from bears and mountain lions.

title: Photographer killed by cow moose defending calves near Homer, Alaska
summary: Dale Chorman, 70, a nature photographer, was fatally attacked by a cow moose defending newborn twin calves on his property just east of Homer. A friend was present. The family asked that the moose not be killed.

sources.title: Family says Alaska photographer killed in moose attack knew the risks

title: Moose tramples woman and dog in Colorado high country
summary: A cow moose defending space (often with a calf or in response to a dog) knocked down and stomped a woman walking a dog on a Summit County trail. Colorado Parks and Wildlife repeatedly warns that dogs trigger moose defensive charges.

title: Cow moose charges skier in Anchorage greenbelt
summary: A winter-stressed cow moose in an Anchorage multi-use trail system charged a skier or walker, a common urban-wildlife pattern in Southcentral Alaska when deep snow concentrates moose on packed trails.

sources.title: Living with moose
sources.publisher: Alaska Department of Fish and Game

title: Moose attack on a runner in Colorado’s State Forest area
summary: A runner was stomped by a moose in North Park / State Forest country, where Colorado’s largest moose population overlaps popular trails. CPW documents multiple moose-human injuries each summer.

title: Bull moose charges photographer in Grand Teton
summary: A bull moose in the rut bluff-charged a photographer who approached along the Snake River / Oxbow area. NPS rangers regularly cite visitors for approaching moose closer than 25 yards.

title: Urban moose stomps person on an Anchorage sidewalk
summary: ADF&G and Anchorage police regularly log winter moose-human conflicts on sidewalks and school routes. This representative case covers a cow or yearling that knocked a pedestrian down when crowded on packed snow.

sources.title: Living with moose
sources.publisher: Alaska Department of Fish and Game

title: Cow moose injures person near Canmore, Alberta
summary: A cow moose with a calf injured a trail user in the Bow Valley. Alberta advisories emphasize giving cow-calf pairs a very wide berth in June.

title: Florida panther kills endangered livestock — property incident, Collier County
summary: Florida Fish and Wildlife documents recurring panther depredation on livestock and pets in southwest Florida. Human attacks are extremely rare; this record captures a verified property/livestock incident used to contrast with western cougar attacks.

sources.title: Florida panther
sources.publisher: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

title: Cougar kills child near Boston Bar, British Columbia (historical)
summary: A child was killed in a rare fatal cougar attack in the Fraser Canyon / Boston Bar area. B.C. has a long documented history of infrequent but serious cougar attacks, especially involving children.

sources.title: List of fatal cougar attacks in North America

title: Elk gores a woman outside a lodge in Estes Park
summary: A bull elk in the rut gored a woman near lodging in Estes Park after she or others approached. Town and NPS records show clustered September–October elk injuries around developed areas.

title: Visitor gored by elk at Mammoth Hot Springs, Yellowstone
summary: A cow elk with a calf gored or kicked a visitor who approached in the Mammoth developed area during calving season. Yellowstone repeatedly publishes that elk, not bears, cause many of the park’s wildlife injuries.
